newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Jan sales revision due late reporting - Ehrlich.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Jan sales revision due late reporting - Ehrlich.

text.p: A large upward revision to retail sales for January had to do with late reporting, particularly by apparel outlets and department stores, a senior U.S. Commerce Department official said Thursday.
U.S. Commerce Undersecretary Everett Ehrlich told Reuters that small and mid-size store sales were unexpectedly strong.
Commerce reported earlier retail sales rose 0.8 percent in February following a revised 1.5 percent gain in January.
The January increase was more than double the originally reported 0.6 percent rise.
Seasonal factors also might have been at play in the January data, Ehrlich said.
"The seasonal adjustment factors anticipate big sales in December followed by low levels in January," he said. "The adjustment probably magnified what we were seeing in the raw data."
Also, he said sales in the early part of this year likely got a boost from ahead-of-schedule tax refunds.
Ehrlich said the strength in sales of durable goods was particularly striking.
"That seems to be consistent with the idea that income-tax refunds were going out ahead of schedule this year," he said.

Still, the sales data, together with other information such as recent employment reports and data on housing and construction, suggested "obvious real strength" in the economy at the start of this year. "The economy is going along close to gangbusters," Ehrlich said.
Ehrlich saw few signs that the economy was slowing down after the brisk 3.9 percent growth rate recorded for the fourth quarter of last year
"The numbers we have had so far suggest (first-quarter) growth higher than three percent," he said, adding it "could be" close to four percent.
However, Ehrlich stressed there are many unknown elements to the first-quarter economic picture, particularly trade.
The Commerce official said that despite the strong growth, there were no signs of inflationary pressures or imbalances in the economy.
